Title: Cyrena.Screens — per-kernel design
Content:
# Cyrena.Screens — durable decisions

## Per-kernel service model (not per-document)

`IScreenInterop` is registered as a singleton in the kernel's `IServiceCollection` by `AssistantPlugin.LoadAsync`. Each chat gets its own `ScreenInterop` instance. Chat A and chat B's screen shares are fully isolated.

Rationale:
- The same document hosts multiple chats. A single module-scope "current source" would be an implicit mutex — picking in chat A would destroy chat B's source.
- Per-kernel scoping falls out naturally from the existing DI structure (each kernel builds its own service provider).
- The AI in chat A always captures from chat A's source because it resolves `IScreenInterop` from chat A's kernel.

## Interop holds the active token

`ScreenInterop` keeps `_active`, `_activeLabel`, `_activeDisplaySurface`, `_activeWidth`, `_activeHeight` as private fields. Consumers never juggle tokens.

- `Functions.ScreenshotAsync()` calls `await _screen.CaptureAsync()` with no token.
- `ScreenShareTool` calls `_screen.RequestShareAsync()` and reads `IsActive` / `ActiveLabel` / `ActiveSource` to render state.
- Switching sources is `RequestShareAsync` (which releases the prior) or `StopAsync` (release only).

## Configure-based wiring (still weird, still required)

`IJSRuntime` is only available inside an active Blazor component lifetime, and kernel services are constructed before any component renders. So the `ScreenShareTool` component must hand its `_js` to the interop via `_screen.Configure(_jsRuntime)` in `OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender)`. Same as before.

## StateChanged event

`IScreenInterop` exposes `event EventHandler? StateChanged` so the toolbar component can re-render when the source changes, is replaced, is stopped, or is revoked. The interop swallows subscriber exceptions so a bad listener cannot break active-state transitions.

## Capture pipeline routes through IFileHandlerFactory

`Functions.ScreenshotAsync` does NOT use `FileReferenceContent` directly. It decodes the data URL to bytes, then `IFileHandlerFactory.SaveAsync(bytes, mimeType, fileName)` — same path as `Chat.razor.OnFilePasted` for clipboard pastes. Resulting `KernelContent` is added to a new `ChatMessageContent(AuthorRole.User, "")` and iterated via `_its.Input = ...; _its.Iterate();`.

## JS surface

`Cyrena.ScreenShare` namespace, no `dotNetRef` callbacks:
- `isSupported()` → bool
- `requestShare(preferences?)` → ScreenOpResult (token, label, displaySurface, width, height on success)
- `captureStream(token)` → ScreenOpResult (dataUrl, fileName, mimeType, size on success; sourceLost=true on revoke)
- `releaseStream(token)` → ScreenOpResult
- (legacy) `releaseAllStreams()`, `listStreams()` — kept for any future bulk teardown / reconnect reconciliation

## Browser security: no getScreens() API

The browser does not expose a way to list available displays from JS. The OS picker IS the enumeration. Past-pick labels (for a re-pick menu) are .NET state and can be persisted to localStorage if needed.

## Connection gate

`AssistantPlugin.LoadAsync` checks `ConnectionInfo.SupportImages` and skips the registration for connections that can't accept image content. A text-only model has no use for a screenshot.

## Legacy models

`ScreenStreamInfo`, `ScreenSettingsPayload`, `ScreenCaptureResult` are leftovers from the earlier N-streams design and are no longer referenced. Candidates for removal once the JS side confirms they aren't needed.
